description: The entry-point kinds step 4 detects. A kind listed here was looked for in every scan stamped with this manifest version, so finding none of it is a result; a pattern under notCovered was not looked for, so its absence means nothing. Same principle as extractor readiness for signals.
authDeclaredScope: auth_declared reports authentication as declared in source and config only. Gateway, reverse-proxy and header-based authentication (an API gateway, an access manager injecting identity headers) are not visible to static analysis, so none_declared is a prompt to review how the entry point is protected, not a security finding.

kinds.label: HTTP controller action
kinds.detects: Public actions on ControllerBase, Controller and ApiController subclasses (directly, through in-project bases, or Ardalis EndpointBase*), or classes marked [ApiController]
kinds.identifiedBy: Verb and composed route — [Route] + verb templates with [controller], [action] and [area] resolved; conventional routing recorded with a null template
kinds.authDeclared: [Authorize] / [AllowAnonymous] on the action and its controller chain; global AuthorizeFilter, MapControllers().RequireAuthorization(), fallback policy

kinds.label: HTTP minimal API
kinds.detects: MapGet, MapPost, MapPut, MapDelete, MapPatch, MapMethods
kinds.identifiedBy: Verb and route, with statically resolvable MapGroup prefixes composed; a prefix in a variable recorded unresolved
kinds.authDeclared: Attributes on the lambda; RequireAuthorization() / AllowAnonymous() on the call and its groups; fallback policy

kinds.label: Razor Page handler
kinds.detects: .cshtml with an @page directive and its PageModel OnGet / OnPost / named handlers
kinds.identifiedBy: Verb, route (from the path under Pages/ or Areas/{area}/Pages/ and the @page template) and handler name
kinds.authDeclared: [Authorize] / [AllowAnonymous] on the PageModel; AuthorizePage / AuthorizeFolder / AllowAnonymousTo* conventions; global filters

kinds.label: WCF operation
kinds.detects: [OperationContract] members of [ServiceContract] interfaces, with the implementing class; ClientBase proxies excluded
kinds.identifiedBy: Contract and operation; hosts from .svc files, ServiceHost in code and CoreWCF builders
kinds.authDeclared: Each endpoint's binding, security mode and client credential type, from web.config / app.config and code; [PrincipalPermission]

kinds.label: gRPC service method
kinds.detects: Overrides on classes deriving a generated Service.ServiceBase

kinds.label: SignalR hub method
kinds.detects: Public methods on Hub and Hub<T> subclasses
kinds.identifiedBy: Hub route from MapHub<T>("/path") and method

kinds.label: Message consumer
kinds.detects: Kafka IConsumer<TKey,TValue>.Consume; MSMQ MessageQueue.Receive / BeginReceive / ReceiveCompleted; MassTransit IConsumer<T>.Consume; NServiceBus and Rebus IHandleMessages<T>.Handle
kinds.identifiedBy: Transport, and the topic, queue or message type

kinds.label: Hosted service
kinds.identifiedBy: Service class; whether AddHostedService<T>() registers it

kinds.label: Scheduled job
kinds.detects: Quartz IJob.Execute; Hangfire RecurringJob.AddOrUpdate; System.Threading.Timer in a hosted service
kinds.identifiedBy: Scheduler, job id and schedule expression as written

kinds.label: Console main
kinds.detects: static Main or top-level statements, in a project with no other entry point
kinds.identifiedBy: The Main method or the top-level statements file

kinds.label: Windows service
kinds.identifiedBy: Service class and name; the OnStart / OnStop / ... hooks it overrides; where ServiceBase.Run starts it

kinds.label: HTTP handler or module
kinds.detects: IHttpHandler, IHttpAsyncHandler, HttpTaskAsyncHandler and IHttpModule in source; .ashx files; <httpHandlers>, <handlers>, <httpModules> and <modules> registrations in web.config, including framework and package types
kinds.identifiedBy: Role (handler or module), type, and a handler's path and verb
kinds.authDeclared: Handlers: web.config <authorization> for the path. Modules: not applicable (they see every request)
kinds.entryClass: request (handlers) / lifecycle (modules, which hook pipeline events at Init)

kinds.label: Global.asax event
kinds.detects: Application_* and Session_* methods on HttpApplication subclasses

kinds.label: OWIN startup
kinds.detects: [assembly: OwinStartup(typeof(X))], the owin:appStartup app setting, or a Startup class with Configuration(IAppBuilder)
kinds.identifiedBy: Startup class, how it is declared, and the middleware it registers
kinds.authDeclared: Not applicable (authentication middleware is listed under middleware)

kinds.label: Blazor routable component
kinds.authDeclared: @attribute [Authorize] / [AllowAnonymous] in the component or on its code-behind

kinds.label: Azure Function
kinds.identifiedBy: Function name and trigger type (HttpTrigger, TimerTrigger, QueueTrigger, ...)
kinds.authDeclared: HttpTrigger authorization level: Anonymous is none declared, a key level is declared. Other triggers: not applicable

kinds.label: Desktop application
kinds.detects: WinForms [STAThread] Main (System.Windows.Forms, Application.Run); WPF Application subclass defined by App.xaml
kinds.identifiedBy: Framework and main form or window

notCovered.note: Intercepts every request; not a handler
The handler it returns is dispatched at run time

notCovered.marker: Button1_Click and siblings wired in markup
notCovered.note: Pages are inventoried; their postback events are not
Often a lambda at the registration site
Script-based functions; attribute-based ones are covered

notCovered.marker: A bespoke base class with handler-shaped methods
notCovered.note: Needs the dispatcher read by hand

entryClasses.request: A caller, message or trigger enters and is handled. What downstream steps count (risk, step 8), snapshot (contracts, step 14) and test (step 15). Only request entry points carry auth_declared.
entryClasses.lifecycle: The process or pipeline starts or wires itself up — bootstrap, not a place external work enters. Inventoried, but never counted as surface, snapshotted or made a test target.

origins.application: The entry point's code is in the repository.
origins.framework: A framework or package type the application only registers (web.config handler and module registrations of types no project declares). Kept — it matters for the move to middleware — but it migrates through its package's own path, not by rewriting.
